label: steps 3-5 in sequences starting with h (or l), after k/j/p/<DEL>
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.003% of steps) that is a narrow conjunction. 88% of activation mass comes from sequences whose first token is h (most of the rest start with l), and it fires only at t=3-5. There are two modes. (1) Copy phase, recall_idx=1, mostly when L=3-4: the input is the echoed first token h right after <DEL>. This is the strongest mode (top examples are h h j <DEL> [h]). (2) Original phase, orig_idx=3: input is o/2/t after a k/j/p-heavy prefix (h k k [o], l j k [o]). Magnitude is highest for L=3 copies of h h x. It never fires at t<3, on the delimiter, or past t=6. The predicate captures about 91% of the mass, but precision is only about 3%: most matching steps (e.g. h n e <DEL> h) stay silent, so the exact token conjunction that drives it is not captured.
